item.title: CUDA Programming Model: Writing and Launching Kernels
item.description:
CUDA Programming Model: Writing and Launching Kernels

The previous note covered the hierarchy: thread, warp, block, grid, and how those map to SMs. This note turns that hierarchy into actual code. By the end, you will have seen a complete CUDA program, understood every line, and know how a host program hands work to the GPU.

CUDA is an extension of C/C++. Most of the code you write is ordinary C++. A small number of CUDA-specific pieces — kernel functions, the launch syntax, a few memory APIs, and built-in thread indices — turn a sequential program into a massively parallel one.
